findings.claim: Hy49 identifies Fr25592 uniquely in this version of MPO; Ant242 identifies29666; Ant99 has five records.
findings.consequence: The Hy49/25592 identifier mapping is not an outstanding ambiguity within the pinned export. Accuracy of the historical association is a different question.

findings.claim: Fr29666 gives an explicit same-codex link to HelsinkiAnt173, while its Hy49 mention requests comparison only. The indexed Finnish updated note explicitly distinguishes accepted Ant242 from suggested Hy49 and Ant99.
findings.consequence: H05 cannot be used as a known positive. Date/layout conflict challenges a previously suggested association; it does not overturn a proven positive or establish physical exclusion.

findings.status: previously published specific placement recovered; not a discovery
findings.claim: Older IV157 descriptive prose places a FinskaCameralia48/ChristiernPhilipssons1610 MaryMagdalene leaf between its ff7and8. Fr10370 is the exact matching account48:7/1610 leaf; the newer note itself supplies that full identifier under suggested Codex1505.
findings.consequence: Preserve a specific testable insertion and the later qualified group assertion, instead of flattening both into generic resemblance. Neither chronology nor actual placement has been verified from both manuscripts.

findings.status: conditional side-label difference, not resolved physical orientation
findings.claim: Finnish IV156/157/173 descriptions place letter signatures on medieval verso and Roman numerals on recto. Fr10370 MPO note instead labels k as1r andII as1v.
findings.consequence: No MPO-specific r/v convention is established. Do not transfer provider r/v or capture ordinals directly into a medieval sequence. Inspect actual top-margin tokens and text succession; different source-side convention, reversal or transcription error are alternatives. See side_convention_note.json.

findings.status: conditional falsification from explicit catalogue positions
findings.claim: IV156f2 andIV157f5 have the same catalogued opening interval hVIII–hIX but different feast contents: Peter/Paul versus JohnBaptist.
findings.consequence: They cannot occupy one unrepeated opening address in a single uniform numbering system if both transcriptions are accurate. Repeated/reset numbering, composite structure or catalogue error remain alternatives. This is not an independent image-based exclusion.

findings.claim: IV156f8 is catalogued at kII–kIII and changes from MaryMagdalene toJames. Fr10370 contains MaryMagdalene and its k/II signatures need orientation resolution.
findings.consequence: After orientation, compare overlapping text positions against IV156f8 and the documented IV157gap. Match precise chants and words, not merely feast names. Source descriptions alone do not settle it.

findings.claim: Finnish prose gives IV15722–23by33.5–35.5cm and IV15622.5–23by32–36cm; the indexed metadata does not identify these as leaf versus written-space fields. MPO distinguishes format from schriftraum1.
findings.consequence: A direct dimension exclusion is unjustified. Transposition and measurement category must be established before comparing these values. The old dimensional caution remains valid.

findings.claim: IV156 updated notes qualify Codex1505 as suggested in one passage but later equate it with IV157 in the same field.
findings.consequence: This is evidence of heterogeneous catalogue assertion levels, not proof that the three catalogue units form one manuscript or that the historical question remains unresolved today.

findings.claim: The local Finnish record raw object holds a manually compiled association summary rather than the original catalogue text; normalize_mpo preserves the Swedish row verbatim.
findings.consequence: Cite the indexed institutional wording and its access status directly. Do not present the hardcoded Finnish summary as a raw institutional API response.
